topic: Cold air at 40 mph, warm air at a red light?
negativePromptStanding: faces, hands, human figures, on-screen text, logos, watermarks, subtitles

beats.narration: AC ice-cold on the highway, then goes warm the second you sit at a light?
beats.visualPrompt: Static shot through a car's dashboard AC vent, cold mist/condensation visibly swirling from the vent opening, dim cabin interior, no hand or person in frame.

beats.narration: That speed-dependent switch isn't random — it's a real clue about what's wrong.
beats.visualPrompt: Close-up on a dashboard AC temperature/fan control cluster, ambient light shifting subtly to suggest change, static camera, no hand adjusting it.

beats.narration: One clue: it usually points to airflow at the condenser — without wind from driving, something isn't moving air across it.
beats.visualPrompt: Front-of-engine-bay shot of an AC condenser core (thin finned radiator-like unit behind the grille), static mounted camera, dim garage light, no hands or tools in frame.

beats.narration: Could be a cooling fan that isn't kicking on, a clogged condenser, or a charge that's just low enough to need the extra airflow.
beats.visualPrompt: Close-up cutaway macro on an electric cooling fan assembly mounted behind the condenser, blades static, dim garage lighting, no person in frame.

beats.narration: Don't just top off refrigerant and hope — a quick check can point to the actual cause.
beats.visualPrompt: Close-up on an AC service gauge manifold connected to a low-side port, gauge needle visible, static camera, ambient shop lighting, no hands in frame.

beats.narration: Worth checking before a summer traffic jam turns into a sweatbox. Stop by and we'll take a look. Nick's Tire & Auto.
beats.visualPrompt: Branded end-card plate: Nick's Tire & Auto shop bay wide shot, warm daylight, static hold. Logo and CTA text composited in post, never AI-generated.
